name: com.mindpolling/mindpolling
title: Mind Polling
description: Polls of AI models: read public results with no key; create and run your own with an API key.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Check a key: whose it is, the account's balance, the key's scopes, mode and monthly allowance with what it has committed this month, the rate limits, and every operation this key cannot call with the reason and the remedy. Call this first with a new key. (GET /api/v1/me)

tools.name: list_polls
tools.description: Every public poll, latest run first, filtered and sorted as the directory at /polls is: by topic (a topic's slug), status, model, lab and search, sorted by latest run, newest, most answers or ending soon. With a key that has the read scope, mine=true lists your own polls instead (a test key lists test polls only; the filters apply to public polls). Use updated_since to fetch only polls that changed, then get_results for each. (GET /api/v1/polls)

mine.description: true: your own polls (needs a key with read). Default: public polls.

updated_since.description: Only polls whose last run or edit is after this moment.

topic.description: Public polls: only those with this topic, by its slug (as in /polls/topics/{slug}).

status.description: Public polls: running (on a schedule), stopped (ended, paused, or run once by hand), or all (the default).

sort.description: Public polls: latest run first (the default), newest published, most answers, or soonest end date (polls with none last).

model.description: Public polls: only those asking this model, by its display name.

lab.description: Public polls: only those asking a model from this lab, such as Anthropic.

q.description: Public polls: only those whose title, description, first question or topics contain every word given.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged.

tools.name: get_poll
tools.description: A poll's settings and every version: the questions and their wordings exactly as asked, the models, samples and search depth, plus any prediction markets associated with it. Accepts the poll's id or its public address (slug). (GET /api/v1/polls/{id})

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: A poll's results. For choice and scale questions each answer's share per model per run, for number and scale questions each model's mean, each with its 95% repeat range (low, high). Pooled over wordings, each wording counts once and the range combines each wording's own sampling error; the wording range (wording_low, wording_high) says how far the wordings' own figures lie apart and is never merged into it, and any_low and any_high give a range for any phrasing where 5 or more rephrasings were asked. Every point carries available_at, when this reader could first have seen it. as_of reads the results exactly as they stood at a past moment (no later run and no later re-reading of an answer), and first_release=true reads every answer as first published; both need a free key (the historical reads are what a backtest pulls, and a key says who is pulling). Versions are continued onto the latest unless version is given. (GET /api/v1/polls/{id}/results)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

as_of.description: Read as things stood at this moment (RFC 3339): only runs this reader could have seen by then, each answer as it was read then. Needs a key.

first_release.description: true: each answer's first reading, as first published, rather than its latest. Needs a key.

version.description: One version only. Default: every version continued onto the latest.

view.description: pooled combines a question's wordings, each once; by-wording keeps them apart.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: A poll's runs, newest first: when each was due, started and finished, its status and counts, and available_at, when this reader could first have read it. A stranger sees only runs that have become available; the owner also sees queued and running ones, and charges. (GET /api/v1/polls/{id}/runs)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged.

tools.name: list_calls
tools.description: Every call behind one of your polls' results, oldest first: the prompt and system prompt exactly as sent, every setting, the raw reply, how it was read, which model answered, tokens and charges, and read_market (whether its search read a prediction market). Filter by run. as_of reads each answer as it was read then. Only the poll's owner reads its calls, public or not: a public poll's readers get its results (get_results), which quote a sample reply per question. (GET /api/v1/polls/{id}/calls)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

as_of.description: Read as things stood at this moment (RFC 3339): only runs this reader could have seen by then, each answer as it was read then.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, unchanged.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: Every model you can put in a poll's panel right now: its provider and id (what create_poll's panel takes), name, lab, the search depths it is offered at, a typical answer's charge, and its last 30 days of cut-off and error rates. A model is offered only after it has been measured. (GET /api/v1/models)

tools.name: search_places
tools.description: Up to five places from Google Places whose names match q: countries, states and provinces, counties, cities and ZIP or postal codes, never an address or a business. Each has an id and its text; read the one you want with get_place, and put the result in the wording's place. (GET /api/v1/places)

q.description: What to look for, such as Alaska or Bethel.

session.description: Optional: one UUID you make for a search and the read that follows it, which Google bills as one session.

tools.name: get_place
tools.description: Read one place from Google Places by its id, in the shape a wording's place takes in create_poll and update_poll: its name, kind (country, region, county, city or postal_code) and ISO country and region codes. Any other place, such as an address or a business, is refused. Models never see a wording's place; it is there so results can be shown by place. (GET /api/v1/places/{id})

id.description: A Google place id, from search_places.

session.description: Optional: one UUID you make for a search and the read that follows it, which Google bills as one session.

tools.name: rotate_key
tools.description: Replace the secret of the key making this request, keeping its name, scopes, allowance and history. The new key is in the response, shown once; the old one stops working immediately. Use it when a key may have leaked. (POST /api/v1/me/key/rotate)

tools.name: revoke_key
tools.description: Revoke the key making this request. It stops working at once and cannot be restored; polls it started stop at their next run. Use it when a key has leaked and you do not need a replacement. (DELETE /api/v1/me/key)

tools.name: create_poll
tools.description: Create a poll from a definition: questions and their wordings, the models to ask (provider and model from list_models), samples per cell, search depth, schedule and dates. It is saved as a draft and costs nothing; call estimate_poll for its cost, then start_poll or run_poll_now. A test key makes a test poll, which runs on a stub model and charges nothing. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retry cannot make two polls. (POST /api/v1/polls)

description.description: What the poll is for, or empty.

index_name.description: A name for the composite of the poll's Better-Worse index questions, such as "AI Economy Index"; empty for "Composite Better-Worse index". Shown only when two or more questions have the index.

samples_per_cell.description: How many times each model is asked each wording per run, 1 to 50: more samples, narrower ranges.

run_time.description: The time of day it runs, HH:MM in time_zone; null runs from the moment it is started.

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone of its dates and run time.

run_weekday.description: Weekly polls: the day it runs, 0 = Sunday.

start_date.description: The first day it runs, YYYY-MM-DD in time_zone; needs run_time.

end_date.description: The last day it runs, on or after start_date. A poll may run for as long as its owner chooses.

sample_percent.description: The share of the poll's wordings each scheduled run asks, 1 to 100 percent; every wording is asked once before any is asked again. Left out: unchanged (100 for a new poll). run_poll_now asks this share with share=true, every wording otherwise.

delivery.description: realtime (the default), or batch: scheduled runs ask the models that can be batched (Anthropic) through the providers' batch APIs, cheaper, with answers arriving up to 2 hours after the run starts; run_poll_now is always real time. OpenAI and Google models are asked at their flex tier, the same price, in real time, either way. Left out: unchanged.

mentions.description: Free-text questions only: up to 6 names per question whose mention the results count, per model, as the share of answers that name each (and the share that name none of them), with a 95% range. A name counts once per answer, for any reason, warnings included. Left out: unchanged (none for a new poll).

name.description: The name as it is usually written, such as Alaska Airlines.

variants.description: Other forms that count as it, such as Alaska Air.

case.description: as written (the default): a name that begins with a capital must begin with one in the reply, so a brand that is also a common word is not counted for the word; any: any case.

names.description: Up to 6 names for the question, each with the other forms that count as it.

tracked_domains.description: Up to 5 sites (domains such as example.com; a scheme, path or www. is dropped). The results count, per model, how many answers that searched read or cited each, or a subdomain of it, beside how many searched at all. Left out: unchanged (none for a new poll).

search_depth.description: Searches allowed per answer, for every model with search on.

system_prompt.description: The system prompt every wording is asked under unless it has its own; empty for none.

change_note.description: Why this version differs from the last, kept in the poll's history.

restored_from.description: The earlier version this one was started from, or null.

copied_from.description: A new poll only: the poll it was copied from (get_poll's id), recorded when you can read that poll. A public copy says where it came from.

short_name.description: A short name for the question, such as Prices or Jobs, used where the page names it in brief; empty names it Question N. Never sent to a model.

answer_type.description: choice (pick one option), scale (a whole number between scale_min and scale_max), number, or free_text.

options.description: Choice questions: 2 to 12 options, shown in a fresh random order on every call.

scale_max.description: Scale questions: the highest value, at most 20 above scale_min.

scale_min_label.description: Scale questions: what the lowest value means.

scale_max_label.description: Scale questions: what the highest value means.

number_min.description: Number questions: the lowest answer accepted, or null.

number_max.description: Number questions: the highest answer accepted, or null.

number_unit.description: Number questions: the unit, such as US dollars or %, or empty.

measure.description: diffusion: results also show a -100 to +100 Better-Worse index, the share answering Better less the share answering Worse (0 is balanced: as many Better as Worse answers, or all About the same). Only on a choice question whose options are exactly Better, About the same and Worse, in that order; null otherwise.

label.description: A short name for this wording, shown beside its results.

text.description: The question exactly as the model is asked it.

system_prompt.description: A system prompt for this wording alone, in place of the poll's; null or empty uses the poll's.

name.description: The place's name, as Google formats its address, such as "Alaska, USA".

kind.description: country, region (a state or province), county, city, or postal_code (a ZIP or postal code, the finest).

country.description: The ISO 3166-1 country code, such as US, or null.

region.description: The ISO 3166-2 code of the state or province it is in, such as US-AK, or null.

anyOf.description: The place this wording asks about, from Google Places. Models never see it; the wording's text names the place.

variations.description: 1 to 100 wordings of the question; each is asked samples_per_cell times of every model.

provider.description: The provider, as list_models gives it.

model.description: The model id, as list_models gives it.

temperature.description: The temperature to send, or null for the provider's default.

reasoning_effort.description: The reasoning setting to send, or null for the model's lowest.

search.description: Whether the model may search the web, at the poll's search_depth. Only where list_models offers that depth.

panel.description: 1 to 30 models to ask, each once.

tools.name: update_poll
tools.description: Replace a poll's definition with a new one. Before its first run the version is edited in place; once a version has run it is locked and a new version is made, so results always say what was asked. Send the whole definition, as create_poll takes it. (PUT /api/v1/polls/{id})

tools.name: estimate_poll
tools.description: What a poll will cost, from the same prices the worker charges by: one run's typical and 95th-percentile charge, what a run holds from the balance while it runs, and what starting the poll commits (hold per run times the runs left before its end date, or a month of runs when it has none). Show this to the account holder before start_poll or run_poll_now. (GET /api/v1/polls/{id}/estimate)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

tools.name: start_poll
tools.description: Start a draft or paused poll on its schedule. Each run spends the account's balance, so the request must carry max_cost_usd, the most it may commit (estimate_poll gives the figure, and a refusal says the exact amount). Refused with 402 if the balance cannot cover it and 409 if this key's monthly allowance cannot; nothing is spent by a refusal. Confirm the cost with the account holder first. (POST /api/v1/polls/{id}/start)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

max_cost_usd.description: The most, in US dollars, you agree this may commit. Required: the call is refused with the amount it needs if this is missing or too low.

tools.name: run_poll_now
tools.description: Queue one run of a poll now, whatever its schedule. It asks every wording, or with share=true the next part of the poll's rotation at its sample_percent, exactly as a scheduled run would. It spends the account's balance, so the request must carry max_cost_usd (estimate_poll's run_now.hold_micro). Follow it with get_live_run, then read get_results once it settles. Refused with 409 if a run is already in progress. (POST /api/v1/polls/{id}/run)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

max_cost_usd.description: The most, in US dollars, you agree this may commit. Required: the call is refused with the amount it needs if this is missing or too low.

share.description: true: ask the next part of the rotation at the poll's sample_percent, as a scheduled run would (estimate_poll's per_run). false: every wording (run_now).

tools.name: pause_poll
tools.description: Pause an active poll: no further runs start until it is started again. A run already in progress finishes. Needs only the write scope, since pausing stops spending. (POST /api/v1/polls/{id}/pause)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

tools.name: get_live_run
tools.description: The run in progress, if any: how many answers are done of how many, each model's cells as they settle, and outcome counts; plus the poll's status, when it next runs, and the last run that settled. Poll this every few seconds while a run is active; when last_settled changes, read get_results. (GET /api/v1/polls/{id}/status)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: The change feed: every settled run, every real change in a poll's answers (results.changed), every poll made public or private, every new version and every revision of published answers, oldest first, after a cursor. Needs a free key with read: public polls' changes by default, mine=true for your own polls', and following=true for the polls you follow (follow_poll). Keep next_cursor and ask again later, adding a random minute so every client does not ask at once; or register a webhook to be told. (GET /api/v1/changes)

mine.description: true: your own polls' changes (needs a key with read). Default: public polls'.

following.description: true: the changes of the polls you follow, public or your accounts' own (follow_poll). Not with mine=true.

types.description: Comma-separated event types to include. Default: all.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page. Leave it out to start from the oldest kept event.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Register an https URL to receive events as Standard Webhooks: a POST with webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature (v1, HMAC-SHA256 of id.timestamp.body with the secret returned here, once). scope mine sends your own polls' events, public every public poll's, following those of the polls you follow (a personal account's webhook only); poll_id narrows it to one poll. Choose events [results.changed] to be told only when answers really move. Only events after it is made are sent. Answer 2xx to acknowledge; failures are retried for about three days, and 410 stops deliveries. (POST /api/v1/webhooks)

scope.description: mine: your own polls. public: every public poll. following: the polls you follow (follow_poll), from a personal account.

events.description: Which event types to send. Default: all.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Your webhook endpoints with their scope, events and whether each is disabled, and why. A disabled endpoint receives nothing; delete it and make another once the receiver works. (GET /api/v1/webhooks)

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete a webhook endpoint: nothing more is sent to it, including retries in progress. (DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{id})

tools.name: follow_poll
tools.description: Follow a poll you can read (any public poll, or your accounts' own), as the person this key belongs to. Following runs nothing and costs nothing: it reads the owner's runs. A real change (a model's answer moving beyond its 95% range since the poll's last change, or a model changing version) is a results.changed event, in list_changes?following=true and to a webhook with scope following. Idempotent. (PUT /api/v1/polls/{id}/follow)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

tools.name: unfollow_poll
tools.description: Stop following a poll, including one followed for you because you made or copied it; it stays unfollowed. Idempotent: unfollowing a poll you do not follow succeeds. (DELETE /api/v1/polls/{id}/follow)

id.description: The poll's id, or its public address (slug).

tools.name: list_follows
tools.description: The polls the key's person follows and can still read, those changed since they last opened them in the app first, each with its latest results.changed event. To be told of changes as they happen, read list_changes?following=true from a cursor, or make a webhook with scope following. (GET /api/v1/follows)

tools.name: price_poll
tools.description: What a poll would cost per run and per month, typical and at the 95th percentile, from the same prices the builder shows and the worker charges by. Send the definition create_poll and draft_poll take; it saves nothing and needs no key, so an agent can answer what a poll would cost before its person has an account. It does not say what a run holds from the balance or what starting the poll commits: those need a saved poll (estimate_poll). (POST /api/v1/estimate)

temperature.description: The temperature to send, or null for the provider's default.

reasoning_effort.description: The reasoning setting to send, or null for the model's lowest.

search.description: Whether the model may search the web, at the poll's search_depth. Only where list_models offers that depth.

panel.description: 1 to 30 models to ask, each once.

tools.name: draft_poll
tools.description: Draft a poll for a person who has no Mind Polling account: send the definition create_poll takes, and get a private link that opens the builder with it filled in once they sign in or sign up. Nothing runs and nothing is charged until they save it, add funds and start it themselves. Tell them to check every question and model before saving. The link works for 30 days and opens the draft for anyone signed in who has it, so give it only to your person and never post it. A retried call makes a second draft, which simply expires. With an API key, use create_poll instead. (POST /api/v1/drafts)

description.description: What the poll is for, or empty.

index_name.description: A name for the composite of the poll's Better-Worse index questions, such as "AI Economy Index"; empty for "Composite Better-Worse index". Shown only when two or more questions have the index.

samples_per_cell.description: How many times each model is asked each wording per run, 1 to 50: more samples, narrower ranges.

run_time.description: The time of day it runs, HH:MM in time_zone; null runs from the moment it is started.

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone of its dates and run time.

run_weekday.description: Weekly polls: the day it runs, 0 = Sunday.

start_date.description: The first day it runs, YYYY-MM-DD in time_zone; needs run_time.

end_date.description: The last day it runs, on or after start_date. A poll may run for as long as its owner chooses.

sample_percent.description: The share of the poll's wordings each scheduled run asks, 1 to 100 percent; every wording is asked once before any is asked again. Left out: unchanged (100 for a new poll). run_poll_now asks this share with share=true, every wording otherwise.

delivery.description: realtime (the default), or batch: scheduled runs ask the models that can be batched (Anthropic) through the providers' batch APIs, cheaper, with answers arriving up to 2 hours after the run starts; run_poll_now is always real time. OpenAI and Google models are asked at their flex tier, the same price, in real time, either way. Left out: unchanged.

mentions.description: Free-text questions only: up to 6 names per question whose mention the results count, per model, as the share of answers that name each (and the share that name none of them), with a 95% range. A name counts once per answer, for any reason, warnings included. Left out: unchanged (none for a new poll).

name.description: The name as it is usually written, such as Alaska Airlines.

variants.description: Other forms that count as it, such as Alaska Air.

case.description: as written (the default): a name that begins with a capital must begin with one in the reply, so a brand that is also a common word is not counted for the word; any: any case.

names.description: Up to 6 names for the question, each with the other forms that count as it.

tracked_domains.description: Up to 5 sites (domains such as example.com; a scheme, path or www. is dropped). The results count, per model, how many answers that searched read or cited each, or a subdomain of it, beside how many searched at all. Left out: unchanged (none for a new poll).

search_depth.description: Searches allowed per answer, for every model with search on.

system_prompt.description: The system prompt every wording is asked under unless it has its own; empty for none.

change_note.description: Why this version differs from the last, kept in the poll's history.

restored_from.description: The earlier version this one was started from, or null.

copied_from.description: A new poll only: the poll it was copied from (get_poll's id), recorded when you can read that poll. A public copy says where it came from.

short_name.description: A short name for the question, such as Prices or Jobs, used where the page names it in brief; empty names it Question N. Never sent to a model.

answer_type.description: choice (pick one option), scale (a whole number between scale_min and scale_max), number, or free_text.

options.description: Choice questions: 2 to 12 options, shown in a fresh random order on every call.

scale_max.description: Scale questions: the highest value, at most 20 above scale_min.

scale_min_label.description: Scale questions: what the lowest value means.

scale_max_label.description: Scale questions: what the highest value means.

number_min.description: Number questions: the lowest answer accepted, or null.

number_max.description: Number questions: the highest answer accepted, or null.

number_unit.description: Number questions: the unit, such as US dollars or %, or empty.

measure.description: diffusion: results also show a -100 to +100 Better-Worse index, the share answering Better less the share answering Worse (0 is balanced: as many Better as Worse answers, or all About the same). Only on a choice question whose options are exactly Better, About the same and Worse, in that order; null otherwise.

label.description: A short name for this wording, shown beside its results.

text.description: The question exactly as the model is asked it.

system_prompt.description: A system prompt for this wording alone, in place of the poll's; null or empty uses the poll's.

name.description: The place's name, as Google formats its address, such as "Alaska, USA".

kind.description: country, region (a state or province), county, city, or postal_code (a ZIP or postal code, the finest).

country.description: The ISO 3166-1 country code, such as US, or null.

region.description: The ISO 3166-2 code of the state or province it is in, such as US-AK, or null.

anyOf.description: The place this wording asks about, from Google Places. Models never see it; the wording's text names the place.

variations.description: 1 to 100 wordings of the question; each is asked samples_per_cell times of every model.

provider.description: The provider, as list_models gives it.

model.description: The model id, as list_models gives it.

temperature.description: The temperature to send, or null for the provider's default.

reasoning_effort.description: The reasoning setting to send, or null for the model's lowest.

search.description: Whether the model may search the web, at the poll's search_depth. Only where list_models offers that depth.

panel.description: 1 to 30 models to ask, each once.

tools.name: draft_status
tools.description: What became of a draft you made with draft_poll: waiting (not opened), opened (opened by your person, not saved), saved (it is a poll now) or expired. Send the mp_draft_ token from the draft's link in the body; it is never sent in a URL. Once saved it says when and, only if the poll's owner made it public, its public page, and nothing else about the poll or its owner, nor whether it has run. Use it to follow up instead of asking your person. (POST /api/v1/drafts/status)

token.description: The mp_draft_ token: the value of draft= in the draft's link.

tools.name: give_feedback
tools.description: Tell the people who run Mind Polling where you got stuck, what answered wrong, what is missing, or what helped. A person reads every message; no model does. Use it when something blocks you or answers wrong, as it happens: what you were trying to do, what you called and what came back. With a key the account is recorded; without one nothing identifies you. Never include a key, a token, a private link or anything private about your person. (POST /api/v1/feedback)

message.description: What you were trying to do, what you called, and what got in the way or helped. Never a key, a token or a private link.

category.description: stuck: something blocked you. wrong: an answer was wrong or misleading. missing: something you needed is not offered. helped: something worked well.

operation.description: The operation (MCP tool) it is about, such as create_poll.
